examples.name: Default
examples.summary: The whole world at medium density. The layer fills its nearest positioned ancestor, so the box it sits in is what gives it a size; `position` parks the map in the room `scale` leaves, and `offsetX` / `offsetY` shift it from there, past the box edge when large enough.

examples.name: Regions
examples.summary: Every region that holds data centers, each lighting only its own over the same whole-world map. `asia` and `oceania` hold none and would read as a bare landmass, so they are left out.

examples.name: Densities
examples.summary: Levels are cumulative: `low` lights 65 data centers, `medium` 186 and `high` 275. `none` draws the landmass alone.

examples.name: Fades
examples.summary: The layer masks itself so it meets copy without a hard edge. `--network-map-fade-start` is where the fade still holds full ink and `--network-map-fade-end` is where it reaches zero, both set from the consumer’s class.

examples.name: Animated
examples.summary: The data centers pulse in three staggered waves. The pulse stops under reduced motion, leaving the data centers static.

examples.name: Traffic
examples.summary: `traffic` draws a mesh between lit data centers: faint grey links and orange packets that grow out of one data center and are absorbed into another, each ray on its own clock. Under reduced motion only the links remain.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same content written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<NetworkMap>` tag into a real `NetworkMap`. Braced attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry and never imports the component. `NetworkMap` is a background layer, so `DocMarkdown` sets it in a framed 2:1 box.
